title: Initialize a repository
requirement: The CLI shall initialize a repository-local Roadmap workspace with the files and directories needed to begin planning work.
acceptance_criteria: From a valid repository, initialization creates a usable workspace; invalid input returns actionable guidance; no partial workspace remains after failure.

title: Manage issues
requirement: The CLI shall support the complete issue lifecycle from capture through archival while preserving identity and history.
acceptance_criteria: A user can create, find, inspect, prioritize, assign, update, progress, close, archive, and restore an issue; close and archive preserve its stable ID, path, workflow history, and relationships.

title: Plan with projects and milestones
requirement: The CLI shall organize work into projects and milestones that communicate scope, sequence, due dates, and progress.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can establish a project and milestone, assign issues by stable ID, inspect scope and derived progress, and close or archive planning artifacts without losing traceability.

title: See and advance current priorities
requirement: The CLI shall help a developer select the most relevant work and advance it through a visible workflow.
acceptance_criteria: The daily view identifies current, overdue, and high-priority work; the developer can start, update, block, review, and complete an item without losing context.

title: Work offline with portable data
requirement: Users shall be able to read and manage core project data without a network connection or proprietary service.
acceptance_criteria: Core issue, milestone, project, configuration, reporting, health, and recovery operations work without network access; canonical data remains human-readable and version-controllable.

title: Automate status from Git activity
requirement: The CLI shall connect Roadmap work to branches and recognized commit activity through explicit, reversible Git integration.
acceptance_criteria: A user can set up integration, link work to a branch, apply a documented commit transition, inspect status, and remove automation without corrupting project data or unrelated hooks.

title: Share canonical roadmap state through Git
requirement: Users shall be able to collaborate on Roadmap state through ordinary Git workflows without configuring or running a Roadmap-managed synchronization backend.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical roadmap files can be committed, fetched, merged or rebased, conflict-resolved, and pushed with standard Git; Roadmap performs no hidden network synchronization and reads the resulting repository state.

title: Use human and machine-readable output
requirement: The CLI shall expose stable human-readable and machine-readable output suitable for terminals, scripts, exports, and stakeholder reports.
acceptance_criteria: Supported commands produce documented rich, plain, JSON, CSV, or Markdown output; machine-readable stdout parses cleanly and contains no presentation noise.

title: Exclude credentials and sensitive data
requirement: The CLI shall keep credentials and sensitive values out of repository data, command output, and routine logs.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap stores no Git or provider credentials and removes legacy credential configuration; sensitive runtime values are never serialized and output and logs are redacted.

title: Diagnose project health
requirement: The CLI shall identify invalid configuration, malformed entities, broken links, naming problems, dependency faults, and storage inconsistencies.
acceptance_criteria: Health results identify the affected entity, severity, evidence, and corrective action and offer stable exit codes or structured output for automation.

title: Recover from destructive changes
requirement: The CLI shall provide confirmation, dry-run, backup, transaction recovery, archive, restore, or rollback safeguards appropriate to destructive operations.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can preview risk, cancel safely, recover a complete old or new canonical state after interruption, and verify that identity and relationships remain intact.

title: Understand and act on failures
requirement: The CLI shall return concise, actionable errors and a non-success exit status when an operation cannot be completed.
acceptance_criteria: Validation, filesystem, local Git, configuration, conflict, and data-integrity failures identify what failed, what changed, and the safest next action without an unhandled traceback in normal mode.

title: Install and verify the CLI
requirement: A supported user shall be able to install the published package and invoke help and version commands without repository-specific environment workarounds.
acceptance_criteria: A clean supported environment installs the release artifact; `roadmap --help` and `roadmap --version` exit successfully; the reported version matches package metadata.

title: Preview initialization
requirement: A user shall be able to preview initialization choices and filesystem changes before modifying a repository.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run reports the intended workspace and initial project actions and creates or changes no files; deprecated template interactive and force controls warn without changing the supported plan.

title: Open or safely reinitialize a workspace
requirement: The CLI shall detect an existing workspace and either open it unchanged or require explicit intent before reinitialization or overwrite.
acceptance_criteria: Normal invocation preserves existing data; force or migration paths display impact, create recovery evidence, and produce a valid workspace or restore the prior state.

title: Inspect and change configuration
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to view validate set and reset supported configuration values within their declared project user or invocation scope.
acceptance_criteria: Valid changes persist in the correct scope and affect subsequent commands; invalid keys values or scopes are rejected; credentials and machine-specific runtime values are never written to project configuration.

title: Create a complete issue
requirement: A contributor shall be able to capture a work item with title description type priority assignee milestone labels estimate and relationships as applicable.
acceptance_criteria: The issue receives a complete stable Roadmap ID and timestamps; supplied fields round-trip; invalid references are rejected; omitted optional fields receive documented defaults.

title: Find and inspect issues
requirement: Users shall be able to list, filter, search, sort, select columns, and view details for open, closed, backlog, blocked, overdue, assigned, and archived work.
acceptance_criteria: Queries use explicit workflow and lifecycle scope; empty results are explicit; stable-ID lookup resolves every retained issue and detail views include relationships and ordinary external references when requested.

title: Prioritize, assign, and organize an issue
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to update issue metadata, assign ownership, and move work between backlog and milestones with a recorded reason.
acceptance_criteria: The intended issue changes once; invalid assignees or milestones are rejected; related milestone and project views reconcile after the change.

title: Manage workflow state and progress
requirement: A developer shall be able to start, progress, block, unblock, move to review, and close an assigned issue using valid state transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Each transition updates status, progress, timestamps, and reason consistently; invalid transitions fail without mutation; closed work appears in completion views.

title: Manage dependencies and critical path
requirement: Users shall be able to add, remove, replace, inspect, and analyze issue dependencies without creating invalid graphs.
acceptance_criteria: Missing targets, self-links, duplicates, and prohibited cycles are rejected; blocking state is visible; critical-path output explains the calculated sequence.

title: Discuss issue work in context
requirement: Users shall be able to add and list comments attached to an issue.
acceptance_criteria: Comments retain stable identity, author, issue target, timestamps, ordering, and optional reply relationships; malformed comment data is diagnosed without corrupting the issue.

title: Preserve implementation context
requirement: A developer shall be able to connect an issue to a local branch and record ordinary implementation, external-reference, and verification context so another contributor can resume it.
acceptance_criteria: The issue detail view exposes retained context by stable ID; an external URL or identifier remains inert canonical content and triggers no provider operation.

title: Review a daily work summary
requirement: A developer shall be able to see assigned in-progress, overdue, high-priority, and recently completed work for the upcoming milestone.
acceptance_criteria: The summary uses the configured identity and next milestone, avoids unrelated work, explains empty states, and offers a verbose view when needed.

title: Create and maintain a project
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to create, inspect, update, close, archive, restore, and delete a top-level project.
acceptance_criteria: Project identity and repository metadata persist; destructive actions require appropriate confirmation; linked milestones remain traceable through close, archive, and restore.

title: Create and maintain a milestone
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to create, inspect, update, and assign a consistently named milestone with description, due date, and optional project.
acceptance_criteria: Naming and dates validate; the milestone has stable identity; assignment is visible from both issue and milestone views.

title: Review milestone scope and progress
requirement: Users shall be able to inspect milestone scope in list, detail, board, and recalculated progress views.
acceptance_criteria: Counts and progress derive from current linked issues; board columns reflect workflow state; empty and overdue milestones are explicit.

title: Close and retain delivery history
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to close, archive, restore, or explicitly purge projects and milestones with clear effects on linked work.
acceptance_criteria: Close preserves workflow history; archive changes visibility without changing status or canonical path; restore reverses visibility without duplication; purge requires explicit confirmation and reports linked-entity impact.

title: Inspect local Git context
requirement: A developer shall be able to inspect repository, current branch, and issue-to-branch context without giving Roadmap remote credentials or installing hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Inspection detects supported local repository context, works with network access blocked, distinguishes available and unavailable state, and gives a safe next action without mutation.

title: Manage Git hooks reversibly
requirement: A developer shall be able to preview, install, configure, inspect, and uninstall Roadmap Git hooks without overwriting unrelated hook behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated install is idempotent; existing hooks are preserved or composed; status reports exact installation state; uninstall removes only Roadmap-managed content.

title: Update work from commit messages
requirement: Recognized commit references shall apply only documented issue transitions and shall ignore unrelated text.
acceptance_criteria: Valid references identify one issue and transition; malformed, ambiguous, or unknown references report or safely skip; repeated processing is idempotent.

title: Create and link an issue branch
requirement: A developer shall be able to create a valid branch for an issue, optionally check it out, and link an existing current branch.
acceptance_criteria: Dirty-tree and branch-collision risks are reported; generated names are safe; force behavior is explicit; subsequent status and issue views show the link.

title: Use repository-owned Git configuration
requirement: A user shall be able to use Roadmap in an existing Git worktree without selecting a Roadmap sync backend or giving Roadmap remote credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap discovers repository context needed for local features while Git remains responsible for remotes and authentication; no provider secret is written to any Roadmap configuration scope.

title: Review roadmap changes with Git
requirement: A user shall be able to inspect Roadmap changes as ordinary human-readable Git diffs before committing them.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical file changes are deterministic and reviewable with standard Git tools; preview requires no Roadmap baseline or remote API call.

title: Exchange roadmap changes with ordinary Git
requirement: A user shall be able to exchange committed Roadmap changes with collaborators using standard Git fetch pull merge or rebase and push workflows.
acceptance_criteria: After Git updates the working tree Roadmap reads the canonical result and rebuilds stale derived state; no Roadmap sync command or provider mapping is required.

title: Resolve concurrent edits as Git conflicts
requirement: A user shall resolve concurrent edits to canonical Roadmap files using ordinary Git conflict workflows rather than a second application merge engine.
acceptance_criteria: Conflicted documents are not accepted as valid state; after the user resolves and stages them Roadmap validates the canonical files and performs no hidden remote reconciliation.

title: Rebuild stale derived state
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to discard and rebuild indexes caches and other projections from canonical Roadmap files.
acceptance_criteria: A missing stale incompatible or corrupt projection is detected; rebuild is idempotent; canonical documents remain unchanged and queries return equivalent results afterward.

title: Attach external references without synchronization
requirement: A user shall be able to attach an external URL or identifier to a Roadmap entity as an ordinary reference without making the external record authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: The Roadmap ID remains canonical; adding editing or removing a reference performs no network operation and creates no baseline mapping or reconciliation state.

title: Inspect roadmap change history through Git
requirement: Users shall be able to audit canonical Roadmap changes with ordinary Git history diff and blame tools.
acceptance_criteria: History identifies committed content changes without a separate synchronization audit store; application diagnostics remain distinct from Git history.

title: Choose stable output formats
requirement: Users shall be able to request supported output formats and columns without changing command meaning.
acceptance_criteria: Rich and plain views remain readable; JSON and CSV parse; Markdown is valid; exit status and stderr behavior remain stable across formats.

title: Export filtered project data
requirement: A user shall be able to export selected Roadmap data in JSON CSV or Markdown to an explicit destination.
acceptance_criteria: The file format and schema are documented; filters match interactive queries; overwrite behavior is explicit; empty exports remain valid.

title: Run actionable health scans
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to scan selected entity types and severities, include dependency checks, group results, and consume stable exit codes.
acceptance_criteria: Healthy, degraded, and unhealthy results map to documented exit codes; each finding identifies entity, rule, severity, and remediation; JSON and CSV parse.

title: Preview and apply targeted health fixes
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to preview and selectively apply safe fixes with confirmation and a post-fix report.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run is non-mutating; only selected fix types run; every mutation is reported and recoverable; a follow-up scan verifies the result.

title: Clean backups and malformed data safely
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to inspect and clean old backups, misplaced files, duplicates, and malformed entities without broad unintended deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted and all-mode previews enumerate exact paths and actions; retention rules are honored; failures are surfaced; recoverable data is preserved.

title: Validate canonical files and derived projections
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to compare canonical files with local indexes and preview projection rebuild or pruning.
acceptance_criteria: Missing, extra, duplicate, stale, or mismatched projection records are reported; repair never overwrites canonical content and confirmed projection state can be discarded and rebuilt.

title: Edit and move canonical data
requirement: Users shall be able to inspect or edit supported canonical files with ordinary tools and move a workspace across supported systems.
acceptance_criteria: Valid manual edits are loaded on the next command; invalid edits produce diagnostics; stable ID-based paths newline and encoding differences preserve entity meaning across supported systems.

title: Restore data after an interrupted or destructive operation
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to identify the relevant backup or interrupted transaction and restore a complete consistent scope without creating duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Restore can be previewed; recovered entities retain stable IDs paths and relationships; the operation reports overwritten or skipped data and supports post-recovery validation.

title: Upgrade and migrate a workspace
requirement: A user shall be able to upgrade the CLI and migrate supported workspace data with compatibility checks, preview, backup, and rollback guidance.
acceptance_criteria: The CLI detects schema/version differences; migration is idempotent; unsupported downgrade or breaking changes stop before mutation and link to a migration path.

title: Create a requirement artifact
requirement: A user shall be able to create an optional user or technical requirement with stable identity, readable key, statement, rationale, priority, owner, lifecycle status and type-specific acceptance or verification criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Draft creation needs criteria rather than passing evidence; defaults are explicit; canonical Markdown and unknown fields round-trip; duplicate identities or readable keys fail explicitly.

title: Find and inspect requirements
requirement: Users shall be able to list, filter, search, sort, and view requirements by type, journey, stage, priority, status, owner, relation, and roadmap target.
acceptance_criteria: Results and JSON are deterministic; detail shows readable key, UUID, current revision, recorded history/evidence and typed relations; missing or ambiguous keys fail explicitly; retained closed or archived targets remain inspectable. Supersession management is deferred.

title: Review and transition requirement status
requirement: A requirement owner shall explicitly transition requirements through Draft, Accepted, In Progress, Verified, Deferred and Rejected without deriving approval or verification from issue closure.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid transitions fail before mutation; transition reasons, attributed actor and timestamps are retained; semantic edits to accepted content require explicit reacceptance; local actor attribution does not imply account authentication.

title: Link requirements to intent, work, and evidence
persona: Product owner, architect, developer, or reviewer
requirement: Users shall be able to create, remove and inspect typed relationships among requirements, implementation issues, project/milestone targets, verification evidence and ordinary external report references.
acceptance_criteria: Each edge has one canonical owner and derived reverse lookup; invalid types, duplicates, missing targets and prohibited cycles are rejected; unlinking preserves artifacts; closed/archived targets resolve; manual broken links are diagnosed. No generic plugin graph or provider synchronization is introduced.

title: Measure traceability and coverage
requirement: Users shall be able to find accepted requirements without planned work, completed work without verification, orphan work, broken relations, and coverage by journey, priority, milestone, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal and versioned JSON use one calculation and list exact eligible IDs for unplanned requirements, unjustified orphan work, completed work awaiting verification, stale/failed evidence, broken links and blocked requirements; counts reconcile; explicit maintenance justification is valid without fabricated product requirements.

title: Record acceptance evidence
requirement: A requirement owner shall record criterion-specific verification evidence bound to the requirement revision and mark it Verified only after explicitly checking its current criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence records criteria covered, result, location, applicable revision/commit/artifact, reviewer and date; missing or failing current evidence refuses verification; acceptance-bearing edits stale prior evidence while preserving history; file existence and issue closure are not passing evidence.

title: Import and export requirements
requirement: Users shall be able to export requirements to CSV and import reviewed CSV changes through a dry-run and conflict-aware transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip preserves supported fields and relations; preview reports creates, updates, invalid rows, and conflicts; failed import leaves canonical files unchanged.

title: Supersede or archive requirements without losing history
requirement: Users shall be able to supersede or archive obsolete requirements while keeping stable references, rationale, relations, and replacement links.
acceptance_criteria: The prior ID remains resolvable and immutable except for status/history metadata; replacement relationships are validated; reports exclude or include historical artifacts explicitly.

title: Build roadmap scope from accepted requirements
requirement: Users shall be able to select Accepted requirements into projects, milestones, or roadmap targets and monitor delivery and verification without conflating requirements with issues.
acceptance_criteria: Only eligible requirements are committed; implementation work remains distinct and linked; scope changes preserve decision history; progress distinguishes planned, implemented, and verified.

title: Configure and safely evolve a workspace
requirement: The CLI shall support configuration and version evolution without exposing secrets, silently changing meaning, or making supported workspace data unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can inspect and change configuration, upgrade the CLI, preview required migration, recover from failure, and reopen the workspace with equivalent supported data.

title: Manage intent through delivery and verification
persona: Product owner, architect, maintainer, or contributor
requirement: Roadmap shall support an optional end-to-end requirements-as-code journey from capture and governance through planning, implementation traceability, evidence, and supersession.
acceptance_criteria: A team can create and approve requirements, link distinct delivery work, identify coverage gaps, record verification evidence, and preserve history using repository-native artifacts.

title: Generate a host-shaped issue, branch, or pull-request link
requirement: A user shall be able to generate a correctly shaped link to the current issue, branch, or pull/merge request for the detected Git hosting provider without Roadmap making a network call or storing credentials.
acceptance_criteria: A distinct read-only hosting URL command (recommended `roadmap git url`, pending CLI contract review) reports a usable URL for recognized GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea remotes; unrecognized or missing remotes produce clear guidance instead of a fabricated link; no credential is read or stored.

title: Visualize schedule and critical path
requirement: Users shall render a dependency-based project or milestone schedule with earliest/latest starts and finishes, all critical paths and slack under explicit planning assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal and JSON reconcile; unlimited parallelism is stated; missing estimates remain unknown unless an explicit default is selected; deadline variance, outside-scope dependencies, cycles and empty schedules have documented outcomes; no assignee-capacity forecast is claimed.

title: Edit requirements without identity or content loss
requirement: Users shall edit requirement fields and Markdown while preserving UUID identity, readable references, user content and revision history.
acceptance_criteria: Rename, update, manual-edit and projection-rebuild journeys preserve identity, unknown frontmatter, body content and links; semantic edits create a new acceptance-bearing revision; write conflicts preserve newer user edits.

title: Explain the next eligible work
requirement: Users shall receive deterministic read-only next-work recommendations using an explicit eligibility and ordering policy.
acceptance_criteria: Only accepted requirements or explicitly justified maintenance are eligible; unmet dependencies are visible; recommendations explain priority, scope, deadlines, unblocking value and verification gaps; identical input/time yields stable JSON/order; no command auto-approves scope or changes priority.

title: Keep requirements optional in existing workspaces
requirement: Existing issue-only workspaces shall retain their supported workflows when requirements support is unused or introduced explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Reads create no requirements or canonical edits; supported 0.3.1 data upgrades with preview/recovery and preserved IDs/content; initialization/issues/planning/export stay usable; unsupported downgrade is explicit; separately declared 0.4 deprecation removals have replacement guidance.

title: Govern Roadmap development with Roadmap
requirement: The Roadmap project shall use its version-controlled workspace to plan, execute and verify 0.4 release work and turn observed workflow friction into traceable development evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Use published 0.3.1 immediately and test candidates in copies; each new implementation item links requirements or maintenance rationale; record task/version/command/expected/actual/workaround/disposition; audit historical data; perform one verified CSV-to-artifact cutover without dual manual authorities; release review includes a self-hosted journey and friction dispositions.

title: Resolve the baseline GitHub backlog through Roadmap
requirement: Every GitHub issue open at the agreed baseline shall have a linked Roadmap work item and an evidence-backed terminal disposition as a verified fix or explicit not-planned closure.
acceptance_criteria: Freeze dated baseline; reconcile existing local IDs and preserve source URLs; track triage/work/verification locally; confirm exact remote identity/state before explicit gh closure; record success/failure; retry without duplicate records; not-planned retains rationale and never counts as implemented coverage; final audit finds no omitted baseline issue; later arrivals receive separate triage.

title: See completed work after merge and pull
requirement: Collaborators shall see an issue completed in Roadmap on their first relevant read after pulling the merged canonical completion record.
acceptance_criteria: Two independent clones exercise close/commit/merge/pull; issue detail/list and milestone/project progress agree despite a stale local projection; IDs/history/context survive; no reimport or manual repair of valid received data is needed; unresolved Git conflicts are diagnosed; issue completion does not verify requirements.

title: Import complete external issue records safely
requirement: Maintainers shall explicitly import selected GitHub issue records completely into Roadmap and repeat imports without losing local work or duplicating records.
acceptance_criteria: Preview selection and repository-qualified identity matching; preserve descriptions, all paginated comments, agreed metadata/timeline and attribution; retain source URLs for attachments without claiming binary capture; use existing local IDs; unchanged input is idempotent; changed input retains attributed source revisions and exposes differences without overwriting local planning/status; validate and recover interrupted writes.

title: Receive GitHub-only completion through the repository
requirement: Collaborators shall receive correct Roadmap completion through the documented next-pull workflow when implementation is merged and the issue is closed only on GitHub.
acceptance_criteria: Define and verify when external closure is captured and committed into pullable canonical data; exact external identity maps to the retained local issue; preserve local fields/history; failed or repeated delivery is visible and safe to retry; conflicting/reopened states follow an explicit reviewed policy; issue completion never implies requirement verification.

title: Publish committed closure decisions to GitHub
requirement: Explicitly opted-in Roadmap closures shall close their exact linked GitHub issues automatically after the canonical decisions reach the default branch.
acceptance_criteria: Preview offline; read pinned committed records only; require qualified target and explicit completed/not-planned disposition and closure reason; publish evidence linked to commit; retry safely after partial failures; skip already closed issues; no automatic reopening or inbound reconciliation; verify simulated failures and a live post-merge run.
